_comment: Upstream unit ids that a ruling ENDED, and the id each became. A published cue pins the unit id that existed the day it was authored; when shireishabbat renames a unit, that pin stops naming anything and the cue silently reports no liturgical position at all -- the Barechu defect, one layer further out. This list is how a pin from before a rename still finds its unit. It mirrors .live's RETIRED_UNITS (scripts/ops/emit-machzor-book.mjs) row for row so the two repos forward the same ids to the same successors; adding a row here is the whole change. A retirement is a permanent fact about an id, so these lines do not expire -- but a successor that is not in the library is refused at load, because a forwarding list whose targets do not exist is the loophole the miss log exists to close. R-0919-audit-1 Wave 2.

retired.why: The capture filed p.147's unit (Un'taneh Tokef) under the name printed on it, K'dushat Hayom, and p.148's B'rosh Hashanah under Un'taneh Tokef. shireishabbat 95a9836 corrected both.
The identical misfiling one service earlier, at pp.56 / 57-58. shireishabbat 10d3a58 corrected it the same way.
Once R6-a decided p.56 is Un'taneh Tokef, the kavannah introducing it is the Un'taneh Tokef kavannah.
The unit's stem gave the moments artifact the id `service` -- unique and meaningless. The corpus renamed the unit rather than special-case the derivation. shireishabbat e5a87e3.

Not a ruled retirement -- a spelling the corpus no longer uses, found here on 2026-09-20 because three published cues (Kedusha 1, 2 and 3) pinned it and reported no position. Verified rather than assumed: `amidah.kedushah@legacy-shabbat-morning` appears nowhere in content/siddur-library.json, `amidah.kdushah@...` does, and the three cues' Hebrew is 98 + 114 + 126 = 338 stripped characters, exactly the 338 of that unit's 33 blocks, each cue's opening falling inside it. Three slides of one unit. shireishabbat's own consumer check names `kedushah` as the reader's divergent spelling of this same unit. If Daniel would rather see a ruling id on this row, it is his to mint; the evidence is above either way.
